Bias-Corrected SMKLE by Extrapolation in the Bandwidth

Source: R/bc_engine.R, R/skmle_bc.R
skmle_bc.Rd

Fits skmle() over a grid of bandwidths, chooses a bandwidth by a plug-in estimate of the mean squared error of the coefficients, and reports the coefficients extrapolated to bandwidth zero. The standard error accounts for the correlation between fits at different bandwidths.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'bc'
print(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'bc'
summary(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'summary.bc'
print(x, ...)

skmle_bc(
  formula,
  data,
  id,
  obs_times,
  s = 0,
  h_grid = NULL,
  n_h = 12,
  degree = 1,
  n_boot = 2000,
  seed = NULL,
  quiet = FALSE,
  ...
)

Arguments

x, object

A bias-corrected fit from skmle_bc(), kee_cox_bc() or kee_async_bc().

...

Further arguments passed to skmle(), such as nknots, maxeval or optimizer.

formula

A model formula. The left-hand side must be a survival::Surv() response and the right-hand side must contain at least one covariate.

data

Data frame containing the variables used in formula, id, and obs_times.

id

Subject identifier. Non-numeric identifiers are allowed and are internally converted to integer subject codes.

obs_times

Longitudinal observation times aligned row-wise with data. Times may be on any scale; the sieve basis and the cumulative-hazard quadrature are built on the observed follow-up, so there is no need to rescale to the unit interval first. h must be on the same scale.

s

Box-Cox transformation parameter, defaulting to 0. s = 0 is the proportional hazards model, s = 1 is the additive hazards model, and values in between interpolate. If you do not have a reason to choose otherwise, the default is the familiar Cox model.

h_grid

Optional increasing vector of candidate bandwidths. If NULL, n_h values log-spaced from \(\max\{\min(X_i - T_{ij} : X_i > T_{ij}),\ \tau n^{-0.6}\}\) to \(\tau = \max_i X_i\).

n_h

Number of candidate bandwidths when h_grid is NULL.

degree

Degree in \(h\) of the bias model and of the extrapolation: 1 (the default) removes the first-order bias of a one-sided kernel, and 2 also removes a term in \(h^2\).

n_boot

Number of simulated grids used to include in var the variability from the data-driven choice of bandwidth. With 0, var is the variance that treats the selected bandwidth and window as fixed.

seed

Optional integer seed for those simulated grids. If NULL, the current RNG state is used.

quiet

Logical; if TRUE, suppress progress output.

Value

An object of class c("skmle_bc", "bc") with components:

  • coefficients, var: the extrapolated estimate and its covariance, including the variance from choosing the bandwidth,

  • var_fixed: the covariance treating the selected bandwidth and window as fixed,

  • h: the selected bandwidth,

  • fit: the skmle() fit at h,

  • window: the bandwidths used in the extrapolation,

  • weights: the matrix of extrapolation weights \(a_j\), one row per grid point and one column per coefficient,

  • grid: a data frame with one row per bandwidth and coefficient giving the estimate, its standard error, the estimated bias and the estimated mean squared error,

  • cov_all: the joint covariance of the estimates over the grid, ordered by bandwidth and then coefficient,

  • n_boot: the number of simulated grids behind var,

  • degree: the degree of the bias model and extrapolation,

  • call: the matched call.

The bias

At bandwidth \(h\) the estimator evaluates the hazard at each time with covariates observed up to \(h\) earlier. The lag acts as measurement error and attenuates the coefficients. For a covariate that changes by jumps, the resulting bias is linear in \(h\), and a small-sample term of order \(1/(nh)\) is added to it. The mean of \(\hat\beta_h\) is therefore modelled as \(\beta_0 + c h + e/h\).

The selected bandwidth

For each coefficient, \(c\) and \(e\) are estimated by a regression of \(\hat\beta_h\) on \((1, h, 1/h)\) across the grid, weighted by the inverse sandwich variances. The selected bandwidth h is the grid point that minimises the estimated mean squared error summed over coefficients, \(\sum_k \{(\hat c_k h + \hat e_k / h)^2 + \widehat{\mathrm{var}}(\hat\beta_{k,h})\}\). fit is the skmle() fit at that bandwidth.

The extrapolated estimate

coefficients is the intercept of a weighted regression of \(\hat\beta_h\) on \((1, h)\) over the grid points in \([h/2, 2h]\). This removes the linear term of the bias. The intercept is a linear combination \(\sum_j a_j \hat\beta_{h_j}\) of the grid estimates, so with the bandwidth and window held fixed its covariance var_fixed follows from the joint sandwich $$\mathrm{Cov}(\hat\beta_{h_j}, \hat\beta_{h_m}) = A_{h_j}^{-1} \Bigl(\tfrac{1}{n}\textstyle\sum_i S_{i,h_j} S_{i,h_m}^\top\Bigr) A_{h_m}^{-1} / n,$$ where \(S_{i,h}\) is subject \(i\)'s score contribution at bandwidth \(h\).

Because the bandwidth and window are chosen from the same estimates, the extrapolated estimate has additional variance that var_fixed omits. var includes it. n_boot grids are drawn from a normal distribution whose mean is the grid estimates and whose covariance is the joint sandwich; the selection and extrapolation are rerun on each simulated grid, and var is the covariance of the resulting estimates. No model is refitted, so this step takes a few seconds. In simulation at \(s = 1\), the data-driven selection added 6–9\ estimate.

The extrapolated estimate has smaller bias and larger variance than the coefficients of fit. Use it with var for confidence intervals.

A selected bandwidth at an end of the grid raises a warning. Grid points whose fit has no usable variance are dropped, also with a warning.

See also

skmle(), skmle_cv()

Examples

# \donttest{
library(survival)
set.seed(123)
dat <- sim_skmle_data(
  n = 150,
  mu = function(tt) 8 * (0.75 + (0.5 - tt)^2),
  mu_bar = 8,
  alpha = function(tt) 0.5 * 0.75 + 0.75 * (tt * (1 - sin(2 * pi * (tt - 0.25)))),
  beta = c(1, -0.5),
  s = 0,
  cen = 0.7
)
bc <- skmle_bc(Surv(X, delta) ~ covariates, data = dat, id = id,
               obs_times = obs_times, s = 0, n_h = 8, quiet = TRUE)
bc
#> Call:
#> skmle_bc(formula = Surv(X, delta) ~ covariates, data = dat, id = id, 
#>     obs_times = obs_times, s = 0, n_h = 8, quiet = TRUE)
#> 
#> Selected h = 0.2757 (plug-in MSE); extrapolated (degree 1) over h in [0.1794, 0.4236]
#> 
#> Bias-corrected coefficients:
#> covariates1 covariates2 
#>   1.8464607  -0.7798997 
summary(bc)
#> Call:
#> skmle_bc(formula = Surv(X, delta) ~ covariates, data = dat, id = id, 
#>     obs_times = obs_times, s = 0, n_h = 8, quiet = TRUE)
#> 
#> Selected h = 0.2757; extrapolated over h in [0.1794, 0.4236]
#> 
#>             estimate std.error      z  p.value estimate_at_h std.error_at_h
#> covariates1   1.8465    0.4855  3.803 0.000143        1.1706         0.2639
#> covariates2  -0.7799    0.4462 -1.748 0.080463       -0.4342         0.3124
# }
